title: observability-sprint-backlog-and-metric-cleanup-plan
content:
Context / why this doc exists:

We have accumulated ~120 dashboard widgets and ~300 unique metrics surfaced across inference-related services (serving runtime, KV cache, routing, dedicated nodes). A lot of these are noisy, redundant, or stale — causing alert fatigue, dashboard bloat, and high query costs. This doc is a working sprint backlog + proposal for a focused metric cleanup and dashboard slimming effort that keeps high-fidelity SLI coverage while reducing dashboard query costs and improving oncall signal-to-noise.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce number of dashboard widgets in the inference dashboards by 40% within 6 sprints (approx 3 months).
- Reduce daily query/compute cost for observability cluster related to inference by 25% in same window.
- Achieve >90% coverage for production SLIs (latency P50/P95, error rate, throughput, KV cache hit) mapped to customer-impacting user journeys.
- Remove or consolidate metrics that have not been referenced in the last 9 months.

High-level approach / principles:
- Customer-impact first: prioritize metrics that can explain user-visible regressions (latency, error, cost, model-fallbacks).
- Metric contracts: every metric we keep must have an owner, a doc blurb, and an alert or dashboard that uses it.
- Tiering: dashboards/widgets will be classified GOLD (service SLI/alert), SILVER (investigation), BRONZE (archival/rarely used). Only GOLD widgets show by default on primary runbooks.
- Cost-aware retention: prefer pre-aggregated counters and rate-based SLI calculations over high-cardinality raw event queries.
- Trace-to-metric mapping: ensure every alerting SLI has an associated trace anchor to speed triage.

Sprint backlog (initial tasks, owners):
- Inventory finalization (Marco): produce canonical CSV of metrics, last_query_date, cardinality, owner, description — due 2025-02-21.
- Tagging pass (Anika): add "tier" tag (gold/silver/bronze), "sli_owner" and "trace_anchor" fields in metric registry — due 2025-02-25.
- Retire unused metrics (Priya): list of metrics not referenced in last 270 days + no owner -> propose retire set -> schedule deletion window (30d soft delete) — due 2025-03-07.
- Dashboard slimming pilot (Ethan): pick two dashboards (serving-runtime-overview, routing-fallbacks) and reduce widgets by 50% following tiering rules; measure cost delta — due 2025-03-14.
- Sampling & retention policy proposal (Marco + SRE): draft adaptive trace sampling tied to token-cost and error-severity — due 2025-03-06.

Metric decision heuristics (quick rules):
- Keep if: directly maps to SLI or used in an active alert; used by >1 dashboard; owner assigned and has a confluence blurb.
- Consolidate if: multiple metrics represent the same concept across services (e.g., "latency_ms" vs "p50_latency"), or they differ only by label set that can be represented as a single metric with sanitized labels.
- Pre-aggregate if: cardinality > 1000 but only aggregate stats are needed for dashboards/alerts -> move to summary counters/quantiles.
- Archive if: last_query_date > 270 days AND no active owner OR replaced by consolidated metric.

Suggested new metric naming guardrails (for future onboarding):
- Use service.prefix.metric_name.unit (e.g., serving.kv_cache.hit_rate.percent)
- Keep label sets small: customer_id only where necessary, otherwise prefer customer_tier or team
- Avoid high-cardinality free-form labels (input_filename, raw_model_hash)

Tracing and sampling notes (proposal):
- Current problem: traces are high volume for tokenized inference requests (many internal spans per token) and we are sampling uniformly which misses important edge cases.
- Proposal: adaptive sampling policy
  - Always keep 100% traces for spans that end with error OR include fallback model routing events.
  - For successful requests: sample using a budget that is divided by token_consumption band (low/medium/high); sample more aggressively for high token requests since they are more costly and often indicate complex flows.
  - Maintain a per-service "trace_budget" (tokens/sec) tracked in observability-controlplane; when budget exceeded, reduce sampling for low-severity traces.
  - Implement severity-weighted tail-sampling: keep proportionally more traces that exhibit high tail latency (P99 window > threshold).

Trace anchors (how to link metric alerts to traces quickly):
- Ensure each alert payload includes a short list of candidate trace IDs by querying recent traces matching the service, route, and request_id within the alert time window.
- Add an automatic sample of top 3 candidate traces to the alert body in Slack/Runbook link.

Dashboard tiering & UX plan:
- GOLD: concise view (4–6 widgets): overall request rate, P95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx split), KV cache hit, current serving capacity vs SLA. These are the only widgets surfaced on the oncall runbook page.
- SILVER: deeper troubleshooting: request distribution heatmaps, model-fallback counts, latency breakdown by step (tokenize, encode, attention, generate), routing decision counts.
- BRONZE: historical/people-facing: long-term trends, owner-specific debug charts, slow query logs. Move these to an archive folder or collapse under collapsible panels.
- Widget cost labels: annotate each widget with an estimated query-cost-per-day and last_accessed_by. Use that to inform removal decisions.

Open decisions / questions:
- What is the acceptable minimum trace sampling rate for successful high-throughput routes? (SRE/infra input needed)
- Are there business-level SLIs we should add beyond latency/error (e.g., hallucination rate from evaluation pipeline)? If yes, who owns the data feed?
- Rollback plan for retired metrics: how long will we keep archival copies and who approves final deletion?

Quick checklist for safe metric removal:
- Confirm no alert references metric
- Confirm no dashboard uses it (search + owners)
- Notify metric owner and team (14d notice)
- Mark metric as deprecated (docs + metric registry) for 30d
- Delete after 30d unless objections logged

Migration/communication plan:
- Week 0: Inventory & tagging (this sprint)
- Week 1–3: Pilot dashboard slimming + sampling changes on staging + run cost experiments
- Week 4: Stakeholder review (alerts owners, product, SRE), freeze for production rollout
- Week 5–8: Rollout incremental retirements (grouped by service) and monitor for 2-week post-change regressions
- Communication: weekly status summary posted to #observability with explicit list of retired metrics and dashboard changes; separate email to CS/Support 48 hours before changes to any customer-facing dashboards.

Rollback & monitoring after retirements:
- Add a temporary "metric-retirement-rollback" alert that triggers if any downstream dashboard panels start returning NaN or if SLI computation steps see >0.5% deviation vs baseline over 24h.

Sample timeline / owners summary (repeatable):
- Inventory: Marco (done by 2025-02-21)
- Tagging: Anika (2025-02-25)
- Pilot dashboard slimming: Ethan (2025-03-14)
- Retire proposals & approvals: Priya (tracks approvals)

Notes to self / freeform brainstorm (informal):
- Could we ship a lightweight "dashboard cost mode" that shows estimated cost impact per widget right in the dashboard UI? That would make prioritization obvious.
- Consider an automated weekly job that reports metrics with zero reads in the last 90 days. Could be useful for other teams too.
- If we standardize metric names across services, it will help cross-service query templates and reduce accidental duplicates (e.g., too many ways to ask for p95).

Recent related artifacts and context links: see linked_artifacts above.

Next meeting: Observability cleanup sync — 2025-02-18 10:00 PT (invite sent). Agenda: inventory review, pilot dashboards selection, trace sampling initial thresholds.

-- end of working doc --
